recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Pop Culture Gnosticism as Hyper Reality", "body": "Chance opened by arguing that popular Gnosticism, from The Matrix to Final Fantasy VII, treated reality as a prison because people judged the world through a media filter. He read an 1823 passage from Godfrey Higgins warning against metaphysical absurdities and a Baudrillard summary of hyperreality. Mario compared religious texts to maps that people trust more than the land, and Lucas argued that splitting science from spirituality produced the same disconnected construct. Chance added that scripture, interpretation and re-interpretation formed a copy of a copy of a copy."}, {"title": "Constellation Writing and Priestly Puns", "body": "Chance presented the idea of lumashi, constellation writing, which he credited to an academic scholar of Mesopotamian astrotheology introduced to him by Gabe. He claimed ancient priest astronomers derived history from the interplay of star patterns and wordplay, and that conquering rulers used it to hand people a divinely approved past. Chance cited Rome's Troy story and the Arthurian round table as examples. One panelist observed that a text with no teacher or oral tradition invited misreading, and Chance warned that treating an allegory as literal history repeated the conquerors' move."}, {"title": "Victim Mindset and the Loosh Farm Question", "body": "Asked for a quick take on what Gnosticism meant, the panel split into personal angles. Gabe described a battle line between the individual and the collective. One of the hosts argued that no layer of victim consciousness runs deeper than believing reality is a loosh farm with nothing good in it. Mario described his own positive outlook, used a fish hatchery analogy to explain why the idea still intrigued him, and said he saw the demiurge and archons as metaphor. Near the end of the show, Gabe called Gnosticism hard core honesty and compared Gnosis to the song of Sisyphus."}, {"title": "Decoding Nag Hammadi, Sophia, and the Demiurge", "body": "Chance broke the name Nag Hammadi into roots he read as serpent, watcher, black and mother or maker, calling this his own interpretation. He noted the translation they used came from a project funded by UNESCO and remarked that this coincided with the creation of the CIA, echoing a link Gabe had raised earlier about the 1947 public release. Chance traced Sophia to wisdom and flowers, read the demiurge as a subordinate workman through Webster's 1828 dictionary, and argued Eve and YHVH shared a name. Mario connected Sophia and the demiurge to Virgo and Mercury."}, {"title": "Geometry, Kabbalah, and Trinities", "body": "Lucas walked the panel through the vesica, claiming it produced the geometric, harmonic and arithmetic means and the musical ratios behind sevens and twelves. Chance mapped the Gnostic aeons onto the Kabbalistic tree, arguing popular Gnostics misread emanations, and Mario noted Malkuth as the lowest sphere and linked it to the earth. Chance then listed Trinities from Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu to Adam and Noah, while Gabe closed by suggesting the archons might simply be numbers that cannot be broken."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight the Horsemen ride to war against the inverted gnosis of Nag Hammadi literalism. Along with LC King, Slick Dissident and Mario Garza, I will be presenting the case that the creation mythos of Cathars, Gnostics, and many modern "truthers" is in fact a fairy tale based on astrotheology and priestly pun-craft. Buckle up.
